trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down-left or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down-left.
I can't rule out up-left or down-left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up-left.
The line must go left: down-left is number 9, which comes later.
Going down-right would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes down-left.
Going right would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes down-right.
Going up-right would force the line onto number 9 before its turn; going right would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going down-right, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-2,2). So the line goes right.
Going up-right would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down-right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-3,2). So the line goes down-left.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-right.
The line must go up-right: right is number 19, which comes later.
Going right would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up-left.
Going up-right would leave both number 9 and cell (-1,-1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up-left.
Going right would turn number 9 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going up-right would force the line onto number 12 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going down-right would leave number 12 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up-left.
Number 12 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down-right would wall in number 22, the last number. So the line goes down-left.

Going left would leave both number 17 and number 16 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would wall in number 22, the last number (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes up-left.
Going down-left would turn number 17 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going down-right would turn number 19 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would turn number 21 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
